insurer: Star Health and Allied Insurance Company Limited

good.name: Room Rent
good.quote: Room (Single Private A/c Room), Boarding and Nursing Expenses as provided by the Hospital / Nursing Home.
good.reference: Section 2 (Coverage) - Section 1(A) and Section 2(A); Schedule of Benefits (Page 9/10) 'In-patient Hospitalization Single Private AC Room'
good.explanation: Hospitalization is covered in a Single Private AC room, including boarding and nursing charges as provided by the hospital. This is a standard room eligibility and helps avoid room rent caps in rupees.

good.name: Initial Waiting Period
good.quote: 30-day waiting period - Code Excl 03 (Applicable for Section 1) ... Expenses related to the treatment of any illness within 30 days from the first policy commencement date shall be excluded except claims arising due to an accident
good.explanation: Illness-related claims are not payable for the first 30 days from the policy start date, except for accidents. This is a standard waiting period, so coverage for new illnesses effectively starts after day 30.

good.name: PED Waiting Period
good.quote: Applicable for Section 1: Expenses related to the treatment of a pre-existing Disease (PED) and its direct complications shall be excluded until the expiry of 36 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy with insurer
good.explanation: Pre-existing diseases are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy inception with the insurer. This means PED-related claims can be rejected during the first 3 years.

good.name: Specific Illness Waiting
good.quote: Specified disease / procedure waiting period - Code Excl 02 (Applicable for Section 1) ... shall be excluded until the expiry of 24 months of continuous coverage after the date of inception of the first policy
good.reference: Exclusions - 2. Specified disease / procedure waiting period - Code Excl 02
good.explanation: Specified diseases/procedures are not covered for the first 24 months from the policy inception date. This can delay claims for listed conditions even if they are not pre-existing.

good.name: Restore Benefit
good.quote: There shall be automatic restoration of the Basic Sum Insured once by 100% upon exhaustion of the limit of coverage during the policy period. It is made clear that such restored Sum Insured can be utilized only for illness / disease unrelated to the illness / diseases for which claim/s was / were made.
good.reference: Special Features - 3(a) Automatic Restoration of Basic Sum Insured
good.explanation: Basic Sum Insured is automatically restored once by 100% after it is exhausted in the policy year. The restored amount can be used only for an unrelated illness, so it won’t help if the same condition needs further treatment.

good.name: NCB
good.quote: The insured person will be eligible for Cumulative bonus calculated at 10% of basic sum insured for each claim free year subject to a maximum of 100% of the basic sum insured.
good.reference: Special Features - 3(b) Cumulative Bonus; Schedule of Benefits (Page 9/10) 'No Claim Bonus 10% for every claim free year maximum up to 100%'
good.explanation: A cumulative bonus of 10% of Basic Sum Insured is added for each claim-free year, up to 100%. This increases your available cover over time if you don’t claim.

good.name: Pre-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Pre-hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 30 days immediately before the insured person is hospitalized.
good.reference: Coverage - Section 1(E) and Section 2(E); Schedule of Benefits 'Pre & Post Hospitalization Expenses 30 days & 60 days'
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered up to 30 days before hospitalization. This is standard and helps pay for pre-admission consultations and tests linked to the hospitalization.

good.name: Post-hospitalization Cover
good.quote: Post Hospitalization Expenses: Medical expenses incurred up to 60 days immediately after the insured person is discharged from the hospital.
good.reference: Coverage - Section 1(F) and Section 2(F); Schedule of Benefits 'Pre & Post Hospitalization Expenses 30 days & 60 days'
good.explanation: Medical expenses are covered up to 60 days after discharge. This supports follow-up medicines and investigations, but longer recovery periods beyond 60 days may not be covered.

bad.name: Consumables
bad.quote: Such associated medical expenses do not include Cost of pharmacy and consumables, Cost of implants and medical devices and Cost of diagnostics.
bad.explanation: Pharmacy/consumables, implants/medical devices, and diagnostics are stated as not included under “associated medical expenses.” This can increase out-of-pocket costs during hospitalization if these items are not covered elsewhere in the policy.

bad.name: Disease Sub-limits
bad.quote: Basic Sum Insured (Rs.) Limit for Cataract Surgery (Rs.) 5,00,000/- 30,000/- per eye and not exceeding 40,000/- per policy period ... 7,50,000/-, 10,00,000/- and 15,00,000/- 40,000/- per eye and not exceeding 60,000/- per policy period
bad.reference: Coverage - Section 1(H); Schedule of Benefits (Page 9/10) 'Cataract Limit...'
bad.explanation: Cataract surgery has a sub-limit of ₹30,000–₹40,000 per eye and an overall cap of ₹40,000–₹60,000 per policy period (based on sum insured). If your cataract treatment costs more, you will have to pay the difference.

bad.name: Modern Treatments
bad.quote: Coverage for Modern Treatments ... is limited to the amount mentioned in table below. This benefit forms part of sum insured. *Sublimits all inclusive with or without hospitalization...
bad.reference: Coverage - Section 1(J) / Section 2(J) reference (Modern Treatments section appears under Section 1 with applicability to both Section 1 and 2); Schedule of Benefits 'Modern Treatments Covered (up to the sub-limits)'
bad.explanation: Modern treatments are covered only up to specified sub-limits and within the sum insured. This can leave a large shortfall for expensive advanced procedures.

bad.name: Co-pay
bad.quote: No explicit co-payment clause found in the provided pages for hospitalization claims.
bad.reference: Policy Wording pages provided (1/10 to 10/10) - Co-pay not stated
bad.explanation: No applied co-pay clause is stated in the provided wording pages. This means you are not required to share a fixed percentage of each admissible claim (unlike many policies that impose 10–20% co-pay).

disclaimer: Standard IRDAI exclusions apply. Please verify all details with your insurer or policy document.
